Calibration of change point models

Source: R/dfr_wwaggr.R
cpd_calibrate.Rd

Post-hoc calibration of the scores of a change point model (indid(), tscp2(), ts2vec()) or of every member of an ensemble (cpd_ensemble()) on labelled sequences, as the WWAggr pipeline does before aggregating: beta calibration (Kull et al., 2017, the method of the paper) or temperature scaling (Guo et al., 2017).

Usage

cpd_calibrate(
  model,
  x,
  labels,
  method = c("beta", "temperature"),
  parameters = c("abm", "am", "ab", "a")
)

Arguments

model

A change point model or a cpd_ensemble.

x

Calibration sequences, in the formats accepted by indid().

labels

Their labels, a 0/1 matrix [sequence, time] (1 from the change on).

method

"beta" (default) or "temperature".

parameters

Parameters of the beta calibration: "abm" (default), "am", "ab" or "a".

Value

A cpd_calibrated model (the model and its calibration map), or a cpd_ensemble of calibrated members.

Details

Every score of every step (the steps without score of the representation models excluded) is a sample, labelled by the label of its step. The beta calibration follows the betacal package used by the reference (https://github.com/betacal/python): a logistic regression of the label on log(s) and -log(1 - s) ("abm"; when one coefficient is negative, the regression is refitted on the other feature alone), on the logit of s ("am"), on log(2 s) and log(2 (1 - s)) without intercept ("ab"), or on the logit without intercept ("a"). Scores are clipped to [eps, 1 - eps] with the machine epsilon of single precision (the reference scores are float32). The regressions are unpenalised (glm; the reference uses scikit-learn's LogisticRegression with C = 1e11).

Temperature scaling divides the logit of the score by the temperature that minimises the log-loss on the calibration data. In the reference code the fitted temperature is stored on the model wrapper and does not change its predictions, so this option follows Guo et al. (2017) rather than the code.

References

Kull, M., Silva Filho, T. M. and Flach, P. (2017). Beyond sigmoids: How to obtain well-calibrated probabilities from binary classifiers with beta calibration. Electronic Journal of Statistics, 11(2), 5052-5080. doi:10.1214/17-EJS1338SI

Guo, C., Pleiss, G., Sun, Y. and Weinberger, K. Q. (2017). On calibration of modern neural networks. Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning, 1321-1330.

Examples

set.seed(1)
make <- function(n) {
  change <- sample(5:24, n, replace = TRUE)
  x <- t(vapply(change, function(c) stats::rnorm(24, ifelse(seq_len(24) < c, 0, 3)), numeric(24)))
  list(x = x, labels = t(vapply(change, function(c) (seq_len(24) >= c) * 1, numeric(24))))
}
train <- make(64)
model <- indid(train$x, train$labels, loss = "bce", epochs = 5, seed = 1)
calibrated <- cpd_calibrate(model, train$x, train$labels)
calibrated$calibrator$map
#>          a          b          m 
#>  0.0000000 86.1514795  0.6543955
